title: SAF upstream PR: delta requirement-first matcher (SRG blocking + CCI tiebreak)
description:
## Description

Patch `@mitre/saf`'s `generate delta` command to replace its single-signal Fuse.js title matcher with a requirement-first record-linkage pipeline. Without this, cross-vendor STIG deltas (RHEL9 -> AL2023, Ubuntu -> RHEL, Win2019 -> Win2022 is a lucky corner case) score ~33% match rate due to vendor-prefix drift in titles pushing identical requirements into the reject band.

This card blocks our `profile-delta` (j64) work: we need a patched local saf (and ideally a merged upstream PR) before running the delta against AL2023 V1R3.

Work done to get here:
- Empirical: current saf produced 62/187 matches on AL2023 V1R3 vs RHEL9 v2.4.0 profile (33%)
- Root cause: `src/commands/generate/delta.ts` mapControls uses Fuse with `keys: ['title']`, threshold 0.3 hard-coded; 121 controls fell in the 0.3-0.4 reject band; 4 extra rejected by 1:1 dedup
- Research: Fellegi-Sunter record linkage recommends deterministic blocking on shared identifiers + probabilistic tiebreak within block (SRG-ID + CCI Jaccard + normalized title)
- Corpus survey: 300-sample of DISA STIG library confirms rule-title prefixes are corpus-derivable (dominant-prefix-before-modal heuristic with 0.5 threshold, returns "" for mixed-prefix corpora)

Branch already created: `feat/delta-requirement-first-matching` in /Users/alippold/github/mitre/saf
Hybrid delta base worktree: /Users/alippold/github/mitre/rhel9-v2r7-plus-gui (V2r7 + cherry-picked GUI/chrony feature work)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **TDD: autoDetectPrefix helper** — unit tests covering (a) RHEL9-like corpus returns "RHEL 9"; (b) corpus with leading "The " returns "The X"; (c) AIX-generic corpus returns "The system"; (d) Google-Chrome-like mixed corpus returns ""; (e) Nutanix-like mixed-subsystem corpus returns short common prefix. Tests red first, then minimal implementation.
- [ ] **TDD: normalizeTitle helper** — unit tests: strips detected prefix when present; returns title unchanged when prefix empty or not at start; handles empty title.
- [ ] **TDD: extractSrgId helper** — unit tests: returns `tags.gtitle` string; returns null when missing; handles malformed tags.
- [ ] **TDD: extractCcis helper** — unit tests: returns Set of CCI strings from `tags.cci`; returns empty Set when missing; dedups within a control.
- [ ] **TDD: cciJaccard helper** — unit tests: identical sets = 1.0; disjoint sets = 0.0; partial overlap correct fraction; both empty = 0.0 (document choice).
- [ ] **TDD: buildSrgIndex helper** — unit tests: groups old-profile controls by their SRG-ID; returns Map; empty profile returns empty Map.
- [ ] **TDD: mapControls rewrite** — Tier 1 (SRG block size 1 + CCI overlap -> deterministic accept); Tier 2 (block size > 1 -> CCI Jaccard rank, emit primary + relateds); Tier 3 (block size 0 -> Fuse fallback with `keys: ['title','tags.gtitle']` and accept threshold 0.45).
- [ ] **Integration test** with AL2023 V1R3 XCCDF + RHEL9 v2.4.0 profile fixture: assert >= 90% match rate (up from 33%).
- [ ] **Regression test**: existing RHEL7 v3r7 -> v3r8 delta fixture still produces same 4/4 match result (baseline of existing test suite).
- [ ] **Output schema**: `delta.json` includes `links` array with `{a_id, b_id, match_method, confidence, relationship, srg}` for each matched pair. Backward-compat: existing `controlMappings` field still present.
- [ ] **Local build + eval loop**: `npm run prepack` builds without errors; `./bin/run generate delta ...` with our AL2023 inputs produces >=90% match rate measured by log counts.
- [ ] **Upstream PR drafted** on `feat/delta-requirement-first-matching` branch with a PR body covering: root cause, research citations (Fellegi-Sunter, Splink blocking), corpus survey summary, before/after numbers, test additions. (Opening the PR is separate; drafting is sufficient for this card.)

## Definition of Done

- All acceptance criteria verified true with evidence in card notes (bd note <id>)
- All TDD cycles documented: test written first, failed, minimal code, passed
- No regression in existing test suite (`npm test` green)
- Before/after match-rate comparison captured as a row in `docs/delta-report.md` on the AL2023 repo when j64 runs
- Card closed only after j64 has successfully used the patched saf

## Workflow

1. `bd update <id> --claim` before starting the rewrite
2. TDD cycle per helper: RED -> GREEN -> REFACTOR, recording the log via `bd note <id>`
3. Rebuild saf locally (`npm run prepack`), point `saf` bin at the local build for testing
4. Re-run `saf generate delta` against AL2023 V1R3 XCCDF + hybrid RHEL9 V2r7+gui profile — capture new match count
5. Draft upstream PR body (URLs to research sources, corpus survey, before/after stats)
6. After all AC pass and j64 has consumed the patched output, close this card
7. **Claude-pace estimate: 90 min** — TDD cycles + build + integration test + PR draft

## Reference

- Design doc (private): `.local/specs/2026-04-20-al2023-inspec-profile-design.md` sections 2 & appendix
- saf branch: `feat/delta-requirement-first-matching` (already created, on mitre/saf checkout)
- Hybrid worktree: `/Users/alippold/github/mitre/rhel9-v2r7-plus-gui`
- Research synthesis (in-conversation, key findings):
  - Fellegi-Sunter probabilistic linkage — Splink docs
  - Blocking key + probabilistic tiebreak pattern standard in record linkage
  - TF-IDF / SBERT noted as future upgrade path; not needed for initial layered pipeline
- Blocks: `profile-delta` (j64)
notes:
SCOPE EXPANSION 2026-04-20 — two items folded into this card.

=== (A) Winston refactor (logger cleanup) ===

The existing `print*` wrappers in src/utils/oclif/cli_helper.ts do TWO jobs:
  1. Apply ANSI color via the legacy `colors` npm package
  2. Append to a module-level `processLogData` array that gets flushed
     to `CliProcessOutput.log` via `saveProcessLogData`

Problems:
- `colors` is unmaintained since 2022 ("Marak incident" — intentional DoS)
- 11 separate `print<Color>` functions is semantic noise over a color lib
- The processLogData array is module-level mutable global state

Considered chalk as replacement: rejected. chalk covers only job #1
(color). We also need job #2 (file sink). Winston is already imported
in saf and has colorized Console transport + File transport — one
library covers both jobs with zero custom abstraction layer.

Decision: replace the 11 `print*` functions + `processLogData` with a
Winston logger that has two transports:
  - Console transport with colorize() (level-based color, per the
    existing `syslogColors` scheme in src/utils/logging.ts)
  - File transport writing to CliProcessOutput.log

Scope:
- ~180 call sites across ~18 files
- cli_helper.ts (104 lines) becomes a small logger factory
- Callers switch from `printYellowGreen('label:', 'val')` to
  `logger.info('label: val')` (semantic) or a thin label/value helper
  if the label:value split needs to survive

=== (B) Tier 2 title-similarity tiebreaker fix ===

Discovered while running the existing Windows 2019 -> 2022 fixture test:
3 old controls in SRG-OS-000480-GPOS-00227 × 3 new controls in the same
SRG, all tagged CCI-000366. CCI Jaccard is 1.0 for all 9 pairs (tied).
My current Tier 2 assigns all 3 new to the first old (first-come-first-
served on ties) -> 1 primary + 2 related = match=3.

Test expects match=5 (each new maps to a distinct old by title meaning).

Fix: Tier 2 must
  - Prefer unclaimed old candidates when multiple candidates have equal
    CCI Jaccard
  - Use normalized-title Jaccard as a tiebreaker so matches land by
    content semantics (e.g. "administrative accounts must not be used"
    on both sides)

New primitive: tokenJaccard(strA, strB) -> 0..1 (TDD'd).

Revised AC: the Windows 2019 -> 2022 fixture test (the "fuzzy logic"
scenario in delta.test.ts) must produce match=5.

=== Revised estimate ===

Original 90 min -> now ~200 min Claude-pace:
  ~20 min  Tier 2 title-similarity fix + tokenJaccard helper (TDD)
  ~60-120 min  Winston refactor across saf
  ~15-30 min  Build unblock (pre-existing TSC errors in convert/* and
             inspec_profile.ts from stale @mitre/hdf-converters types —
             not caused by this PR; decide: exclude in tsconfig, use
             --noEmitOnError false, or fix them)
  ~10 min  Real-data eval (AL2023 V1R3 vs RHEL9 V2r7+gui)
  ~10 min  PR body draft

Still to execute: all the above items.
Phase 1 COMPLETE (Tier 2 title tiebreaker fix + tsx devDep fix for stale-lib trap). Phase 2 COMPLETE (createDeltaLogger factory, full sweep of print* across delta.ts/update_controls4delta.ts/hdf2csv.ts/ckl_metadata.ts, cli_helper.ts deleted, colors dep still referenced only in emasser — followup card created). Branch has 8 commits. 49/49 tests green. Remaining: build unblock, real-data AL2023 eval, PR body draft.

Remaining on card 2u4: (1) real-data eval on AL2023 V1R3 XCCDF + /Users/alippold/github/mitre/rhel9-v2r7-plus-gui hybrid profile to measure before/after match rate; (2) cross-vendor integration test fixture under test/sample_data/ asserting >=90% match; (3) delta.json links[] structured output; (4) upstream PR body draft with research citations + 300-STIG survey summary + before/after numbers; (5) build-unblock decision re pre-existing TSC errors in convert/* and inspec_profile.ts (NOT caused by this PR). ~75 min Claude-pace to complete. Recommended order: 3 -> 2 -> 1 -> 4 -> 5.
[2026-04-21] REAL-DATA EVAL COMPLETE — patched delta exceeds 98% target.

Command: NODE_ENV=development ./bin/run generate delta -X <AL2023 V1R3 XCCDF> -J /tmp/rhel9-hybrid-profile.json -c /Users/alippold/github/mitre/rhel9-v2r7-plus-gui/controls -o /tmp/al2023-patched-run -M -T rule -r /tmp/al2023-patched-report.md

title: First vanilla EC2 eval and pin vanilla.threshold.yml
description:
## Description

Run the complete AL2023 profile against a vanilla AL2023 EC2 instance via `kitchen-ec2`, produce a `results.json`, and pin `vanilla.threshold.yml` to the observed compliance numbers. Many checks will fail on a vanilla system (that's expected and correct) — the pinned threshold becomes the floor for regression detection.

This card validates that the profile runs end-to-end on a real target: no Ruby/InSpec errors, every control produces a result (pass/fail/skip), and `inspec exec` completes within a reasonable wall time.

See design doc §3 test harness, §4 release ladder v0.5.0.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bundle exec kitchen test vanilla` completes end-to-end: create → converge → verify → (optionally) destroy, without tool errors
- [ ] `results.json` produced by the verify phase, captured as an artifact (committed to `.local/` or attached to the card — not to `docs/` since it's a point-in-time snapshot)
- [ ] Summary stats documented: total controls, passed, failed, skipped, error (expect most to fail on vanilla)
- [ ] `vanilla.threshold.yml` committed — pinned to current numbers with explicit pass/fail/skip counts and a regression-protection ceiling (e.g., "failed.total.max: <current+2>")
- [ ] No `inspec exec` errors (as distinct from failed controls); every control returns a status
- [ ] `docs/vanilla-baseline-summary.md` committed with the run summary and timestamp

## Definition of Done

- All acceptance criteria verified with command output in card notes
- Threshold YAML validated by `bundle exec inspec compliance upload --no-compliance-upload --profile-path . --threshold vanilla.threshold.yml` (or equivalent) — passes against the just-captured results
- The kitchen instance is destroyed (no lingering EC2 resources)
- Card closed via `bd close <id>` after verification

## Workflow

1. `bd update <id> --claim` before starting
2. Run `bundle exec kitchen test vanilla`; capture the results.json and summary stats
3. Write `vanilla.threshold.yml` based on observed numbers; validate it parses
4. Commit threshold + summary doc; verify AC + DoD
5. `bd close <id>`
6. **Claude-pace estimate: 45 min** (includes AWS instance boot + full profile eval wall time)

## Reference

- Unit: `vanilla-eval`
- Blocked by: card `profile-cleanup` AND card `kitchen-harness`
- Blocks: card `ci`

title: Adapt ~28 non-strong-match AL2023 controls (epic)
description:
## Description

Adapt the ~28 AL2023 controls that `saf generate delta` did not strong-match to RHEL9 analogs. For each control, rewrite the Ruby body using the AL2023 STIG fix text as primary source, with the nearest RHEL9 V-ID (listed in `docs/controls-status.md`) as a reference pattern. Typical divergences are package/service names, file paths, and systemd unit differences.

**This is an epic.** Once card `profile-delta` closes and the 28-rule list is fixed, this epic splits into 3-4 batch child cards of ~7 controls each (sp:5, 60-90 min per batch). Batch cards are grouped by theme where possible (e.g., "audit + auditd rules", "package install/absence rules", "sudo/privilege-escalation rules").

See design doc §2 data flow step 4, §4 release ladder v0.4.0 ("multi-card — expect 3-4 cleanup batches").

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All 28 non-strong-match controls have hand-written `describe` blocks grounded in AL2023 STIG fix text (not RHEL9 placeholder code)
- [ ] Each adapted control is cross-linked in `docs/controls-status.md` with `status: adapted` and the STIG rule reference (`AZLX-23-*`)
- [ ] Any control that genuinely does not apply to AL2023 is marked `impact: 0.0` with a documented reason (cited STIG language or MITRE policy note) — no silent skips
- [ ] `bundle exec inspec check .` still passes cleanly after adaptation
- [ ] `bundle exec rubocop --autocorrect-all` still clean
- [ ] Batch child cards created, each claimed and closed independently; this epic closes only when all children are closed

## Definition of Done

- All acceptance criteria verified across all batch child cards
- `controls-status.md` reflects final adaptation state (no rows left as `needs-adaptation`)
- No `inspec check` or `rubocop` regressions
- Profile runs end-to-end without errors (tested via ad-hoc `inspec exec` against the running kitchen instance from card `kitchen-harness`)
- Card closed via `bd close <id>` only after every child batch card is closed

## Workflow

1. `bd update <id> --claim` on the epic to own the coordination
2. Create batch child cards via `bd create --parent <this-epic-id> ...` once the 28-rule list is stable (right after `profile-delta` closes)
3. Each child follows its own claim/close cycle
4. Close this epic when all children are closed and AC are verified
5. **Claude-pace estimate: 180 min ceiling** for the epic (split to 3-4 cards of 60-90 min each in practice)

## Reference

- Unit: `profile-cleanup`
- Blocked by: card `profile-delta`
- Blocks: card `vanilla-eval`
- Parallels: card `kitchen-harness` (no shared blocking)
notes:
[2026-04-21] Pre-populated hand-adapt queue from the patched delta run on AL2023 V1R3 vs hybrid RHEL9 V2r7.

Out of 187 target controls: 186 mapped (92.5% primary, 7.0% related), 1 no-match. Of the mapped, **11 flagged as "Potential Mismatch"** by the algorithm (low CCI Jaccard in SRG block OR low Fuse confidence). Plus the **1 genuine no-match** = 12 controls that need human review/hand-adapt.

=== 11 flagged matches (need content review) ===

Tier 2 (SRG block + CCI Jaccard — picked something in the SRG block but content overlap weak):

| Rule (new) | From (RHEL9) | CCI Jaccard |
|---|---|---|
| SV-274018 | SV-257796 | 24% |
| SV-274022 | SV-257943 | 0%  |
| SV-274023 | SV-257944 | 0%  |
| SV-274061 | SV-258125 | 33% |
| SV-274077 | SV-258140 | 33% |
| SV-274133 | SV-258111 | 33% |
| SV-274136 | SV-258112 | 33% |
| SV-274139 | SV-258101 | 13% |
| SV-274160 | SV-258048 | 33% |

Tier 3 (Fuse fallback — no SRG overlap, matched on normalized title alone, below confidence threshold):

| Rule (new) | From (RHEL9) | Fuse confidence |
|---|---|---|
| SV-274146 | SV-258047 | 68% |
| SV-274175 | SV-257945 | 68% |

=== 1 no-match (needs hand-written control) ===

- SV-274030 / AZLX-23-001090: "Amazon Linux 2023 must manage excess capacity, bandwidth, or other redundancy to limit the effects of information flooding types of denial-of-service (DoS) attacks"
- SRG-OS-000142-GPOS-00071 — zero RHEL 9 coverage
- Novel AL2023 DoS-resilience requirement. No ancestor in RHEL 9.

=== How to work this queue ===

For each flagged match: open the generated control in /tmp/al2023-patched-run/controls/, compare its carried-forward describe block against the AL2023 STIG fix-text (from the XCCDF), decide whether to (a) keep, (b) adapt, (c) scrap and rewrite, or (d) mark N/A.

For the no-match: write from scratch using the XCCDF fix-text.

=== Blocked until j64 ===

These IDs can be staged for review but actual hand-adapt waits on card j64 (patched saf merged, delta committed to AL2023 repo).

title: Clone RHEL9 kitchen-ec2 harness to bring AL2023 vanilla box online
description:
## Description

Clone the RHEL9 baseline's `kitchen.ec2.disa.yml` pattern into this repo and point it at a vanilla Amazon Linux 2023 AMI. Goal of this card: `bundle exec kitchen create vanilla` brings up a running AL2023 EC2 instance so the team can iterate on controls via ad-hoc `kitchen login` + `inspec exec` while the cleanup epic runs in parallel.

See design doc §3 test harness. Uses `t2.small` (~$0.023/hr) and `SAF_PIPELINE_SUBNET` env var, mirroring the RHEL9 baseline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `kitchen.yml` committed — default driver (ec2), verifier (inspec), transport (ssh), pointed at the profile in repo root
- [ ] `kitchen.ec2.yml` committed — explicit `vanilla` suite definition: owner `amazon`, AMI name pattern `al2023-ami-*-x86_64-*`, instance type `t2.small`, SSH user `ec2-user`, subnet via `ENV['SAF_PIPELINE_SUBNET']`
- [ ] `kitchen.inputs.yml` committed — minimal baseline inputs the profile needs for a kitchen eval (can start empty if none are required)
- [ ] `bundle exec kitchen list` shows a `vanilla` suite with driver `ec2` and no errors
- [ ] `bundle exec kitchen create vanilla` successfully boots an AL2023 instance (screenshot of `kitchen list` showing `Created` in card notes)
- [ ] `bundle exec kitchen login vanilla` SSH's into the instance and `cat /etc/os-release` reports `Amazon Linux 2023`
- [ ] Docs: add a one-paragraph "Local test box" section to `README.md` describing the `kitchen create vanilla` + `kitchen login` + `kitchen destroy vanilla` flow

## Definition of Done

- All acceptance criteria verified with command output captured in card notes
- Running instance destroyed via `bundle exec kitchen destroy vanilla` before closing the card (don't leave billable resources up)
- No AWS credentials committed anywhere in the repo (all via env or IAM role)
- Card closed via `bd close <id>` after verification

## Workflow

1. `bd update <id> --claim` before starting
2. Test with `kitchen create` / `kitchen login` / `kitchen destroy` cycle; confirm no residual resources
3. Verify AC + DoD, then `bd close <id>`
4. **Claude-pace estimate: 25 min** (includes one full kitchen create + destroy cycle; some wall time is AWS-bound)

## Reference

- Unit: `kitchen-harness`
- Blocked by: card `profile-delta` (profile dir needs to exist so `inspec check` passes; we don't need cleanup complete)
- Blocks: card `vanilla-eval`
- Parallels: card `profile-cleanup` (this card brings the test box online so cleanup work can use it)

title: Run saf generate delta and commit 187 AL2023 controls
description:
## Description

Run `saf generate delta` with the **hybrid RHEL9 V2R7 + feature-branch improvements worktree** (`/Users/alippold/github/mitre/rhel9-v2r7-plus-gui`) as the base profile, and the AL2023 V1R3 XCCDF as the new guidance. This is the fastest path to a runnable AL2023 profile — ~159 of 187 controls will inherit RHEL9 Ruby bodies (including the new best-practice GUI/dconf/gnome_settings libraries from the feature branch cherry-picks).

Capture the delta's markdown report (`-r docs/delta-report.md`) and commit the 187 generated `controls/*.rb` plus an auto-generated `docs/controls-status.md` index.

See design doc `.local/specs/2026-04-20-al2023-inspec-profile-design.md` §2 data flow step 3. Expected outcome: ~159 carried, ~27 needs-adaptation stubs, ~1 blank (V-273999).

**Delta base**: `/Users/alippold/github/mitre/rhel9-v2r7-plus-gui/` — V2r7 tip + 3 cherry-picked commits (`752f7b2` GUI resources, `d9117d8` Copilot feedback, `de56f78` chrony CCI fix). Includes the `libraries/{dconf,gnome_settings,gui}.rb` resources and `INSPEC_CONTROLS_BEST_PRACTICES.md` / `INSPEC_CORE_RESOURCE_PATTERNS.md` — the latter two inform card `profile-cleanup` (ao0) as the authoring rubric for the ~27 adapted controls.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `inspec json /Users/alippold/github/mitre/rhel9-v2r7-plus-gui | jq . > /tmp/rhel9-hybrid-profile.json` produces a valid profile.json
- [ ] `saf generate delta` invocation run with `-X` = AL2023 V1R3 XCCDF, `-J /tmp/rhel9-hybrid-profile.json`, `-c /Users/alippold/github/mitre/rhel9-v2r7-plus-gui/controls`, `-o controls/` (into this repo), `-M`, `-T rule`, `-r docs/delta-report.md`
- [ ] `controls/*.rb` committed — 187 files, one per AZLX-23-\* rule
- [ ] `docs/delta-report.md` committed — `saf generate delta -r` output with per-rule match decisions
- [ ] `docs/controls-status.md` committed — one row per control: `AZLX-ID | status (carried/needs-adaptation/stub) | RHEL9 V-ID matched | notes`
- [ ] `bundle exec inspec check .` passes with zero errors
- [ ] `bundle exec rubocop --autocorrect-all` completes clean
- [ ] `inspec.yml` inputs reviewed; either populated with RHEL9-inherited inputs or explicitly noted as "pending per-control review in card ao0"

## Definition of Done

- All acceptance criteria verified true with command output captured via `bd note <id>`
- Zero `inspec check` errors, zero uncorrectable `rubocop` offenses
- Exact `saf generate delta` invocation is pasted into card notes so the run is reproducible
- Commit message on the resulting commit follows project convention: `feat: delta-generate 187 AL2023 controls from V2r7+gui hybrid base`
- Card closed via `bd close <id>` after verification

## Workflow

1. `bd update <id> --claim` before starting
2. Record the exact `saf generate delta` invocation in card notes
3. Verify AC + DoD (particularly `inspec check` and `rubocop`), then `bd close <id>`

notes:
DISCOVERY 2026-04-20 — blocked on saf upstream patch.

Ran `saf generate delta` with hybrid V2r7+gui worktree as -c, AL2023 V1R3 XCCDF as -X, profile.json via InSpec 7. Output: 62/187 matches (33%), 125 pure stubs, 4 dedup-rejected.

Root cause (confirmed by reading delta.ts source and CliProcessOutput.log):
- Fuse.js matcher uses keys: ['title'] only (not tags.gtitle / SRG-ID, despite comment claiming otherwise)
- Hard-coded accept threshold 0.3 — rejects 121 matches that scored 0.3-0.4 (vendor-prefix drift: "RHEL 9" <-> "Amazon Linux 2023")
- 1:1 dedup rejects 4 more where one RHEL9 rule is split into N AL2023 rules

Fix scoped as a new card: saf-patch (new card to block this one). Uses layered Fellegi-Sunter pipeline: auto-detect corpus prefix -> SRG-ID block -> CCI Jaccard tiebreak -> Fuse fallback with dual keys + 0.45 threshold.

Re-run this card against the patched saf once the patch card closes. Expected: >= 90% match rate (up from 33%).

title: Produce AL2023 vs RHEL9 structural diff report (hdf-diff)
description:
## Description

Run a structural requirement-level diff between the AL2023 V1R3 and RHEL9 V2R7 HDF Baselines using `@mitre/hdf-diff` primitives (or a small wrapper script), render as markdown, and commit to `docs/al2023-vs-rhel9-diff.md`. The report is both a planning input (informs `saf generate delta` flag choices) and a permanent v0.2.0 documentation artifact.

Match strategy: **CCI primary** with **fuzzy-title Jaccard fallback** (≥0.45 threshold); upstream SRG-OS-\*-GPOS-\* group titles carry additional confidence.

See design doc §2 data flow step 2. Expected shape: ~159 strong matches, ~27 CCI-only, ~1 no-match.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/al2023-vs-rhel9-diff.md` committed with a per-rule table: AL2023 V-ID → matched RHEL9 V-ID (if any) → match strategy used → confidence/Jaccard score
- [ ] Summary counts section at the top (strong / CCI-only / no-match buckets), with severity breakdown (CAT1/CAT2/CAT3)
- [ ] The ~28 non-strong-match rules are listed explicitly by AZLX-23 ID + title so the cleanup card has its input list
- [ ] Recommended `saf generate delta` flags (`-T rule|group|version`, `-M` on/off) captured in a "Decisions" section of the diff report
- [ ] `scripts/build-diff.sh` committed (alongside `build-baselines.sh`) making the diff reproducible

## Definition of Done

- All acceptance criteria verified true with evidence in card notes
- `docs/al2023-vs-rhel9-diff.md` renders cleanly on GitHub (markdown lint clean)
- `scripts/build-baselines.sh && scripts/build-diff.sh` produces the committed diff report byte-for-byte (or documented why not, e.g., timestamp lines)
- No regressions in `rubocop` / `inspec check`
- Card closed via `bd close <id>` after verification

## Workflow

2. Keep decisions and caveats in card notes as you discover them (e.g., "chose -T group because ...")

title: SAF follow-up: sweep emasser  usage, drop colors dep
description:

title: Codify profile-delta workflow as a Claude skill (RHEL/Debian/SLES/AMZN/Rocky pipeline)
description:
## Description

Codify the cross-vendor STIG profile-derivation workflow (learned via the AL2023 pilot) as a reusable Claude Code skill. The skill accepts a target STIG XCCDF and a "base" InSpec profile, runs the patched saf delta pipeline, and delivers a best-effort derived profile ready for human review.

Motivation: we have a list of profiles to update/derive (RHEL next, Debian, SLES, AMZN/AL2, Rocky). Each one benefits from the same saf patch + workflow. Codifying the steps in a skill turns "spend a day per profile" into "hand Claude the two inputs and get a reviewable baseline."

## Prerequisite — must run the AL2023 pilot first

This card cannot start until the AL2023 workflow is proven end-to-end (card 2u4 merged upstream, j64/oji/ao0/dtf/dws closed on the AL2023 board, v0.5.0 released). The skill codifies patterns we can only identify after running the full cycle at least once.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Skill lives under `~/.claude/skills/profile-stig-delta/` (or the appropriate plugins dir if contributed upstream)
- [ ] Accepts two inputs: target XCCDF path, base profile path (InSpec profile dir)
- [ ] Automated steps the skill runs:
  - [ ] Auto-detect vendor prefix on both sides (reuses `autoDetectPrefix` from saf)
  - [ ] Call patched `saf generate delta` with SRG-block + CCI-tiebreak pipeline
  - [ ] Produce `delta-report.md` AND `controls-status.md` (auto-generated, one row per control)
  - [ ] Identify non-strong-match controls and produce a hand-adapt queue with STIG fix-text pre-filled
  - [ ] Run `bundle exec inspec check .` + `bundle exec rubocop --autocorrect-all` and report any errors
  - [ ] Optionally (user flag) spin up a kitchen-ec2 instance for iterative dev
- [ ] Documents the workflow as markdown instructions the skill injects into the agent's context
- [ ] Skill references the research that anchors the algorithm (Fellegi-Sunter, SRG-blocking) so future maintainers understand why it works
- [ ] Exercised on at least one second profile (RHEL10 delta, Debian 12 STIG, or similar) before closing

## Definition of Done

- Skill committed, installed, and runs end-to-end on two distinct OS profile derivations (AL2023 being the pilot, one other chosen from the list)
- Hand-off runs: user types `/profile-stig-delta <xccdf> <base-profile>` and gets a reviewable result directory with delta report, controls-status, adaptation queue, and lint-clean profile
- Lessons learned from the AL2023 pilot documented in the skill's agent instructions

## Workflow

1. `bd update <id> --claim` only after AL2023 v0.5.0 is merged
2. Rewatch the AL2023 pilot's full cycle; identify every repeatable step and every decision point
3. Write the skill as agent instructions + reference scripts
4. Exercise on a second profile (user choice — RHEL10, Debian 12, Rocky 9, etc.)
5. Close when the second profile confirms repeatability
6. **Claude-pace estimate: 180 min** (includes one second-profile exercise)

## Reference

- Pilot project: `amazon-linux-2023-stig-baseline`
- Long-term queue (in user's priority order): RHEL (10 when published), Debian 12, SLES (15/16), Amazon Linux 2 STIG refresh, Rocky Linux 9
- Depends on: card 2u4 (saf patch merged upstream)
- Blocks: no cards on this board; enables future profile-creation work

title: CI pipeline: check + lint + rspec + scheduled kitchen-ec2
description:
## Description

Add a GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) that runs `inspec check` + `rubocop` + `rspec` on every PR and push to `main`, plus a scheduled (and manually-dispatchable) kitchen-ec2 vanilla run that validates against `vanilla.threshold.yml`. AWS credentials flow via OIDC federation to an IAM role — no long-lived keys in repo secrets.

See design doc §5 CI pipeline, §4 release ladder v0.6.0.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.github/workflows/ci.yml` committed — job `profile-check` runs on PR + push-to-main: Ruby 3.1 setup, `bundle install`, `bundle exec rubocop`, `bundle exec inspec check .`. Target runtime <2 min.
- [ ] Job `profile-unit-spec` runs on PR: `bundle exec rspec spec/` (no-op if no tests exist yet). Target runtime <1 min.
- [ ] Job `kitchen-ec2-vanilla` runs on `schedule` (nightly cron), `workflow_dispatch`, and push to release tags: AWS OIDC auth, `bundle exec kitchen test vanilla`, threshold-validate against `vanilla.threshold.yml`, `results.json` uploaded as artifact. Fails the workflow on threshold regression. Target runtime <20 min.
- [ ] Summary PR comment posted by the scheduled job with pass/fail/skip counts (via `actions/github-script` or similar — no external Slack dependency for now)
- [ ] No AWS keys or long-lived secrets in `secrets.*`; OIDC trust relationship documented in card notes (or `docs/ci-setup.md`)
- [ ] README gains a CI status badge for the `ci.yml` workflow

## Definition of Done

- All acceptance criteria verified with a real PR run (self-merged PR is fine — just prove the workflow fires)
- A scheduled run has executed at least once successfully
- `results.json` from the scheduled run shows pass/fail matching `vanilla.threshold.yml` baseline
- Card closed via `bd close <id>` after verification

## Workflow

1. `bd update <id> --claim` before starting
2. Open a draft PR early to iterate on workflow YAML (GitHub Actions only runs in a branch)
3. Confirm OIDC trust is set up on the AWS side; document the role ARN used (no ARN in the repo itself — reference via `secrets.*`)
4. Verify AC + DoD, then `bd close <id>`
5. **Claude-pace estimate: 45 min** (some of this is GitHub Actions iteration wall time)

## Reference

- Unit: `ci`
- Blocked by: card `vanilla-eval`
- Terminal card in the v0.6.0 milestone chain

value: AL2023 baseline is the PILOT for a repeatable cross-vendor STIG profile-derivation workflow. Long-term vision (card 9fh): Claude Code skill that takes XCCDF + base profile → best-effort new profile. RHEL 10, Debian 12, SLES 15/16, AMZN 2 refresh, Rocky 9 are downstream beneficiaries.

Delta pipeline uses Approach 2 (diff-first informs delta). hdf-libs XCCDF-benchmark→Baseline conversion feeds ID mapping that informs saf delta flags. Approach 1 (delta-first) rejected because re-runs waste cleanup work if flags wrong.
Emasser colors sweep deferred to card 3uo (separate PR, post-merge of 2u4). Keeps the delta PR focused. colors dep stays in saf until 3uo lands.

tsx devDep is the root-cause fix for stale-lib/ test trap. oclif-core's tsPath auto-rewrites lib/commands→src/commands when NODE_ENV=test AND tsx/ts-node loadable. @oclif/test sets NODE_ENV=test already. Pattern from oclif/oclif, oclif/test, salesforcecli/plugin-data.

AL2023 delta base is hybrid worktree: origin/V2r7 (latest RHEL9 STIG content) + cherry-picked GUI/chrony improvements from user's feature/inspec-best-practices-gui-resources branch (commits 28d1c6d, bbca925, 955325d). V2r7 rule IDs win on conflicts.

inspec-parser at /Users/alippold/github/aesirsystems/inspec-parser — MITRE Ruby gem, parses InSpec profiles via RuboCop-AST into model objects, enables surgical edits via TreeRewriter (preserves formatting). Use during card ao0 (hand-adapt weak-match controls) and future derivations.

Tier 2 composite scoring: 0.7 × cciJaccard + 0.3 × tokenJaccard(normalized-title). Prefer unclaimed candidates; fall back to claimed (→related) only when all taken. Reported confidence = pure CCI Jaccard so semantics stay clear.

Winston over chalk for saf delta logging. print* wrappers do TWO jobs (color + file-sink); chalk covers only color. Winston already a saf dep; Console+File transports cover both in one library with zero custom abstraction.
mapControls rewrite chose full replacement (Option B) not pre-pass adapter (Option A). Cleaner final form, 1:N split primary/related semantics require restructured match loop anyway.
